title: Optimizing Heterogeneous-Agent General Equilibrium
research_question: Can a canonical incomplete-markets heterogeneous-agent economy satisfy individual optimization, rational expectations and general equilibrium with sufficiently accurate numerical solutions?
feasibility_hypothesis: Baseline: established in standard Aiyagari/Huggett-type economies, subject to the specified asset and aggregate-risk closure.
mechanisms: Incomplete-markets household saving and labor decisions
Competitive firms, wages and asset returns
Stationary equilibrium and optional aggregate uncertainty with rational forecasting
state_variables: aggregate shocks and prices, when active
required_equations: Goods, labor and bond/capital market clearing
comparison_baseline: Canonical representative-agent or no-idiosyncratic-risk economy under the same primitives
acceptance_tests: Firm optimization and zero-profit/distributional profit allocation
Asset supply and goods/labor clearing to documented tolerances
Distribution normalization, stationary moments and grid convergence
Krusell-Smith forecasting accuracy if aggregate risk is activated
stage_gate: Accept a fully converged and economically closed baseline; do not add nominal rigidity yet.

implementation.method: equilibrium solving plus ABM/distribution verification when relevant
tests: EGM Euler/KKT and all accounting conditions
